newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bank CCB to launch Belgium's biggest IPO on Nov. 4.
newsitem.headline: Bank CCB to launch Belgium's biggest IPO on Nov. 4.

text.p: Belgian bank Credit Communal de Belgique/Gemeentekrediet (CCB) said on Monday it would issue up to 29.5 percent of its capital starting on November 4 in the country's largest-ever initial public offering.

CCB confirmed that as part of the operation, which forms an integral part of its alliance with Credit Local de France, it would also sell an additional five percent of its shares to Belgian insurance company SMAP/OMOB.
CCB and CLF plan to join forces to create Europe's 22nd largest banking group, which will operate internationally under the brand name DEXIA.
The issue price for the maximum 12,666,454 shares being sold will not be fixed until November 20, the day they are due to begin trading on the Brussels Stock Exchange.
But analysts estimate the offering and SMAP/OMOB placement will together net CCB's existing shareholders - Belgium's towns and municipalities -- around 30 billion Belgian francs ($960 million).

"The price...will be based largely on the price of CLF Holding shares on the Paris stock exchange, after having taken into account the likely impact of a payment of an exceptional dividend and the application, if any, of a differential," CCB said in a statement.
By mid-morning on Monday CLF, which has said it will pay a 25.50 French franc exceptional dividend ahead of the alliance, was trading down 4.5 francs at 435.3, or 2,655 Belgian francs ($85).
Excluding the 1,835,718 shares already placed with SMAP/OMOB, CCB said it aimed to sell 5,966,083 shares to institutions both in Belgium and abroad, and 3,212,507 shares to Belgian retail investors.

CCB said the syndicate of banks arranging the issue would also be able to subscribe to an additional 1,652,146 shares to meet any extra demand and stabilise its share price, should that prove necessary.

The offer to institutions will start on November 4, and open to retail investors on November 8, when CCB will publish an indicative offer price, the bank said in a statement. The offer closes on November 15.
CCB said it had applied to the Brussels Stock Exchange to be listed under the name DEXIA-CC.
